messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING: KV cache fragmentation spike detected in us-west-2 runtime-pool-3. 90th/99th token latency climbing, multiple workers OOM'ing. Alert: kv_cache.freeable_frag_ratio > 0.75 for 5m. thread=3240056789

dena_oncall: ack. paging in. I'm taking lead. Can someone confirm customer impact? any 5xx spikes or 503s?

amy_support: seeing a jump in inbound tickets referencing timeouts and 503s since 10:02 UTC. ~12 tickets so far, two marked P1 (enterprise customers). Dashboard: 502/503 rate up ~8x on that region.

mike_runtime: grabbing logs. initial indicator looks like continuous-batching change from the last deploy increased per-request KV allocation patterns. lots of small slab allocations then fragmentation. stack traces show cudaMalloc failures on a subset of GPUs. snippet:

```
# logs from runtime-pool-3
E 2026-03-15T10:03:12Z gpu0 runtime kv_cache.cc:451 OutOfMemory: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
W 2026-03-15T10:03:12Z gpu0 runtime allocator.cc:293 slab allocation failed, freeable_ratio=0.82
E 2026-03-15T10:03:13Z api gateway request=xxxx status=503 latency=12030ms
```

mike_runtime: we're seeing that when continuous-batching groups seqs differently after the quantization PR, the allocator creates many small KV slices leading to arena fragmentation.

raj_ml: that PR also increased batch window and allowed longer prefilling, right? Could be causing more simultaneous KV growth and less reuse. Suggest short-term: reduce batch window and force prefix cache eviction for hot models. Medium-term: tune allocator arenas.

sara_ops: can we hotfix by reverting the batch window change? If it's a config flip, should be quick. I'll prepare a rollback patch. @mike_runtime can you prepare a canary throttle (reduce max_concurrent_batching to 1 for pool-3) so we stop the aggressive coalescing?

mike_runtime: on it. Applying a runtime config patch to runtime-pool-3: `max_concurrent_batching=1` and `batch_window_ms=4` (was 25). will patch and bounce only affected pods.

deploy-bot: deploying config patch to runtime-pool-3 (patch id: cfg-324005-01). rolling restart pods (3/10 done).

mike_runtime: patch applied to 7/10 pods. early metrics show 99th latency dropping, fragmentation metric trending down: freeable_frag_ratio -> 0.46.

amy_support: ticket volume slowed. no new P1s in the last 8m. customers on pooled plans still reported transient degraded quality but most requests are returning.

carlos_sre: good quick move. we should also run arena compaction on the affected hosts to reclaim fragmentation ASAP. On systems using PyTorch CUDA allocator, env var tweak helps: `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:32,garbage_collection_threshold:0.6` can reduce fragmentation. I can push a node-level init script to set this for pool-3 nodes.

dena_oncall: preference? rollback batch config + node-level allocator tweak + forced compaction? what's the risk of compaction on live GPUs (latency spike)?

carlos_sre: compaction is not free; small transient latency hit possible. we should stagger across nodes and do it during the current lower traffic window; also throttle compaction with a sleep between nodes. I'll coordinate.

raj_ml: also consider evicting large unused prefixes. we can call the cache admin API: `/admin/cache/evict?policy=prefetch-heavy&ratio=0.6` to prune older entries. That should shrink KV working set.

sara_ops: i'm pushing rollback of the continuous-batching PR in the canary. rolling back the code change in canary runtime image and keeping batch_window smaller. deploy-bot will handle image revert.

deploy-bot: initiating image revert for runtime-canary (image: rwd/runtime:v2.9.1 -> rwd/runtime:v2.9.0). canary restart 1/2 succeeded.

mike_runtime: monitoring telemetry. fragmentation metrics improved on patched nodes. OOMs dropped to zero on rolled pods. latency 99th down to baseline within ~6m of patch.

amy_support: customers updated: 2 enterprise customers were affected for ~18m each. Support sent incident advisory to those accounts and offered to sync with their infra teams. No data loss observed.

dena_oncall: ok — running the planned node compaction in staggered batches now. compaction script:

```
for node in pool-3-node-{1..10}; do
  ssh $node 'echo compact > /sys/gpu/allocator/command' && sleep 45
done
```

dena_oncall: starting first 3 nodes. will report back with post-compaction metrics.

mike_runtime: after first 3 nodes compaction, freeable_frag_ratio dropped to ~0.22 on those nodes. request 5xxs remained low.

carlos_sre: pushed PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF to pool-3 node group via instance config. will watch for regressions.

raj_ml: follow-up action: add automated guard rail to prevent batch_window > 10ms if `kv_cache` fragmentation metric > 0.4. We can add a routing policy to throttle long windows.

sara_ops: i'll open a JIRA for rollback postmortem and required automation: ticket RWD-INC-9876. includes steps to add the guard rail and add automatic cache eviction rule.

amy_support: closing customer-facing advisory draft for signoff. will wait until we green across all nodes.

deploy-bot: canary image revert completed (1/1). full pool revert scheduled in 15m if metrics stay stable.

dena_oncall: monitoring 15m window. so far stable: last 10m 5xxs at baseline, fragmentation cluster average 0.18. I'm going to handoff to follow-up ops now. If anything spikes, re-pager.

dena_oncall: handoff -> sara_ops for postmortem and long-term mitigation.

sara_ops: ack. I'll coordinate with runtime + SRE + ML teams. Next steps: run weekly arena compaction for high-churn models, add guard rail for batch_window vs frag metric, and add a canary test that simulates continuous-batching patterns.

mike_runtime: logging actions and saving snapshots of kv cache telemetry for the incident report.

amy_support: marking affected customers and followups in the CRM.

carlos_sre: closing node compaction sweep; all nodes back to normal.

dena_oncall: incident state -> mitigated. moving to post-incident review. closing thread unless anyone needs more. :white_check_mark:
